public_api_additions.note: Streaming getter/putter interfaces are optional; ObjectStore byte methods remain the compatibility surface. ErrStreamingUnsupported must be returned before consuming a request body so callers can safely fall back.

Optional SQL recovery seams provide generation-fenced Session appends, explicit interrupted-run repair, read-only Tool Journal lookup, atomic canonical completed-result delivery, recovery prefixes, and V3 SQL-local sidecars, plus an authorization epoch read/fence. A V3 sidecar is immutable historical delivery evidence beside one canonical tool/result; it does not authorize continuation, consume/ack recovery state, or enable automatic recovery. SQLQueuedPrincipalResolver is a native, same-authority queued-owner resolver; its stable non-disclosure errors let a server distinguish permanent account identity/state failures from retryable storage failures. These are SQL-authority capabilities, not authorization grants for arbitrary external or in-memory control planes.
M1d3 durable host opening and CAS composition checkpoints; non-empty recovery checkpoints fail closed.
M1d4 restart recovery rebinds journal-evidenced resources, loses prior leases, and never substitutes Activate.
M1f1 acceptance proofs are kernel-minted after the tool journal/model gate; zero or mutated proofs fail closed.

M1e1 authorization-first, request-idempotent fencing. Legacy ModuleHost.Fence remains compile-compatible but fails closed; MemoryFenceJournal is a bounded reference, and v35 SQL FenceJournal is provided by pkg/adapter/sql/fencejournal. PostgreSQL v35 Fence verification passed against isolated disposable schemas on 2026-09-04 when HARNESS_TEST_PG_DSN was configured; without that DSN future runs remain an explicit skip. TTLs above 30s and legacy HostGeneration=0 do not guarantee external exactly-once.

Accepted bounded M1 ownership/lifecycle seam: durable host claims are generation-fenced, with a 30s default TTL and 5m maximum. ReleaseOwnership/Close are ownership-only and do not imply module cleanup; legacy zero HostGeneration is compatibility-only.
M1 registration metadata seam only: emits validated runtime collection metadata for a provider. Catalog, router, auth, model resolution, and protocol binding remain M2 concerns.
M1 registration metadata seam only: emits validated runtime collection metadata for a protocol. Provider compatibility, transport, catalog, router, and auth remain M2 concerns.

Accepted bounded process-local, non-recoverable core.Plugin compatibility facade. Declared runtime provides are trusted metadata; no durable effects or legacy Install replay. Full legacy-plugin migration/removal remains later.
Slice A durable resource-migration contract plus the storage-neutral runtime/copy port. Concrete object stores, route barriers, copy policy, and S3 clients remain outside the application package.

Experimental application-level orchestrator seam. It reuses core turn/session DTOs; sequential delegates only to an injected core.Runtime. Registry factories are cheap, side-effect-free boundaries and panics become ErrFactoryPanic. One ID has one active version; upgrade uses a new ID or drains then rebuilds the registry. Profile and database resolution remain in upper layers, and Graph is not registered or enabled here.

M2-A experimental immutable catalog-to-provider-plan metadata contract. A closed bounded snapshot independently binds catalog wire/capability/credential evidence, provider endpoint and implementation evidence, protocol implementation evidence, explicit compatibility, and deterministic snapshot revision. It has no SDK, HTTP, secret value, default global registry, routing fallback, factory, runtime object, or server wiring. Keyless local providers use an empty CredentialRef; dynamic refresh is explicit replacement by an upper layer; real protocol execution and cross-protocol handoff remain M2-B.

Storage bridge for the storage-neutral artifactmigration runtime. It owns DynamicObjectStore, concrete candidate stores, and storage.ArtifactCopyOptions; none of those types cross into pkg/app/artifactmigration.

Slice A SQLite/PostgreSQL persistence adapter for the bounded artifactmigration contract. It requires the v36 schema already initialized by storage.OpenSQLSessionStore and owns no copier or backend client.

Experimental Graph-G1 SQLite/PostgreSQL checkpoint and HistoryStore. It requires storage schema v41 and atomically persists a mutable CAS head with immutable checkpoint versions and append-only transition evidence; no executor, lease, server, or provider wiring is implied.

Graph-G0 is a stdlib-only definition and static-validation contract. Definition revision binds every node kind, state reducer, and conditional predicate ID plus exact registry version, but not a G1 implementation locator or composition revision. It has no executor, checkpoint/store, run/resume, approval/session events, telemetry, provider/protocol binding, transport, workflow adapter, or sandbox implementation. G1 must fail closed when multiple conditional edges are true.

Single profile-ID validator shared by profile registry, session creation, and profile-admin transport. It accepts the built-in bare general ID as well as safe namespaced IDs; it does not relax scope or ownership checks.

Reviewed 2026-09-07 architecture exception: one exact mounted-layer replacement preserves the slot order and existing unmount closure under the registry lock. It is not a multi-layer Release/Canary projection swap or an authorization fence.

public_packages.note: Durable Graph approval adapter over injected approval/checkpoint readers; it owns no storage protocol mutation.
Projects bounded Graph events into core telemetry without payload or identity disclosure.
Strict notification-target HTTP DTOs. Opaque configuration is accepted only on mutation requests and is never projected into responses.
Read-only, metadata-only sandbox discovery DTOs. The projection never returns provider objects, host or mount paths, configuration, credentials, or raw unavailable causes.
Independent Anthropic Messages HTTP provider/protocol registrations; it is explicit and not a default server selection.

Experimental adapter from M2-B normalized events to the existing core.LlmAdapter vocabulary. It collapses lossless tool deltas only at the legacy core boundary; it does not resolve models or own transport.

OpenAI-compatible M2 protocol adapters. HTTPProvider owns endpoint/auth/client reuse; ChatCompletionsProtocol and ResponsesProtocol own their distinct wire payload/SSE or single-response normalization. Exact plugin registration selects protocol; Anthropic Messages is a separate adapter package.
Composition seam from stored model settings to exact immutable execution bindings; it keeps private cache keys out of artifact evidence.

N0 adapter exposing notify.channels, notify.targets, and notify.send as normal core capabilities. It requires the core accepted-invocation proof, derives run identity from guarded context, marks send as approval-required but non-idempotent until a channel proves durable deduplication, and never exposes URLs or credentials to the model.
Explicit experimental Graph runexecutor registration; no server default wiring is implied.
SQL-backed encrypted opaque notification-target configuration; metadata list records omit configuration.

Bounded immutable registry for dynamic-capability runtime factories. It exact-resolves ID/version, defensive-copies requests and manifests, contains factory panics, and has no global registry or transport policy.

Optional context-budgeting, deterministic extractive compression, rolling archival and bounded LLM summarization policies. The app package implements the small core ModelContextAssembler seam without background workers or durable writes outside the supplied session event path.

Credential-free immutable provider/protocol catalog view for transport and settings layers. View.Defaults, Compatible, and Assess distinguish unknown references from known incompatible pairs; implementations remain in adapter packages and retain private factories.

Experimental M2-B protocol-neutral execution contract. Exact catalog snapshot/provider/protocol implementation bindings are fail-closed; Provider owns endpoint/auth/transport and Protocol owns wire body/parser. Credential material is short-lived, non-serializable and clearable. No core bridge, HTTP implementation, server/DB wiring, default registry, or protocol fallback is in the app package.

N0 provider-neutral notification contract: immutable exact-version registry, opaque target refs, bounded non-secret delivery/receipt metadata, panic isolation, provider-error sanitization, and no transport, credentials, persistence, globals, reflection, or background workers.
Shared deadline-aware liveness scheduler with no per-run ticker or goroutine; callbacks remain explicit fail-safe boundaries.

Core keeps only the narrow ModelContextAssembler request/result seam. Context budgeting, token estimation, rolling summaries, extractive summarization, and LLM summarization live in pkg/app/contextassembly.

Experimental Graph-G1 executor with explicit bindings, context planner, segment lease, approval, observer, and sandbox-authorizer ports. The server composes SQL checkpoint/segment adapters but sequential remains the default; sandbox nodes reject without an injected authorizer/provider.

A bounded exact-version provider registry protects callback panics and sanitizes provider failures. Local registration is composition-only and may report unavailable by platform; a normal process is never represented as a sandbox. The Windows current-user Basic provider is the explicit restricted-child path: it requires an ordinary Medium source, reports Host without network isolation, and never falls back to host execution. Historical private control-plane bindings are not part of the current public runtime inventory.

Stdlib-only Graph/Context contract. It defines static graph validation plus bounded mutable checkpoint-head, immutable checkpoint-version, transition, and approval evidence. Store remains the hot CAS port; HistoryStore is an optional read capability. CheckpointVersionOrigin distinguishes same-run commits, v40 migration floors, and future fork lineage; execution bindings, scheduling, providers, transport, and sandbox implementation live in sibling packages and remain separately composed.

Legacy single-action NewCapability remains source-compatible. NewStandardCapabilities separately exposes memory.recall (read), memory.remember (write), and approval-gated memory.forget (write); all derive scope from the accepted principal context.
NewStandardSearchCapability is the guarded standard rag.search variant: it requires accepted invocation and sanitizes index errors/panics; legacy NewSearchCapability remains compatible.

LeaseRequest.HostGeneration, LeaseIdentity.HostGeneration, Lease.Identity.HostGeneration, and FenceRequest.HostGeneration are generation-fenced boundaries; legacy zero generation remains compatibility-only and does not guarantee downstream external exactly-once.

http_notes: The Go mux uses /v1/resources/{key...}; the verifier normalizes it to the OpenAPI /v1/resources/{key} form.
OpenAPI and registered route parity is checked by scripts/verify-openapi.

Generic settings GET is fail-closed for every key; found values are redacted/write_only and never returned. Generic settings PUT requires a present non-null value; explicit empty JSON strings remain valid.

core_budget.public_api_ast_rule: go/ast counts exported top-level names, exported methods on exported receiver types, named exported struct fields on exported types, and named exported interface methods; embedded unnamed members are excluded; *_test.go and generated files are excluded. The historical 2026-09-04 production-line baseline remains 8,615. On 2026-09-07, the reviewed AgentProfileRegistry.ReplaceExact architecture exception raised the exact API ceiling from 909 to 910 and the line ceiling from 8,743 to 8,821 for an 8,817-line implementation; it leaves no API slot and only four fixed line slots. This is not a rolling rebaseline. A separate 1,500 non-blank physical-line ceiling prevents concentration in a single core file.
